note: Curated presets. Coordinates: lat (deg, south negative), lonE (deg east, -180..180). quality: region | exact | approximate.

sites.name: Haworth
sites.notes: Bbox midpoint (lon -34.98 to -12.36, lat -87.39 to -86.11). Retained in 2024; the 2024 map box is larger (~31 km) than other boxes. A peak adjacent to the Haworth crater PSR (IAU -87.45/-5.17, 51 km); elevation -2900 to +1650 m; described as near-perpetual sunlight on the high point (Astronomy.com). PGDA has a 5 m LOLA DEM for Haworth.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.notes: Bbox midpoint (lon -5.66 to 5.15, lat -86.33 to -85.63). Retained in 2024 (digitized -85.97/-0.2). = Mons Malapert (IAU 2024, -85.98/-1.67, 67 km) / Mazarico Site 23. Bussey 2010: M1 86.04S/2.7E 74% (54-95%), M2 86.00S/2.9W 74% (58-90%). LUPEX/ESA ROIs MP1 (85.9756S, -2.11E) and MP2 (86.0265S, 2.76E). Rises to ~5000 m with near-perpetual sunlight on the high ground and nearly continuous Earth view

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.notes: Digitized from NASA's Oct-2024 map (box ~17 km). Coincides with the 2022 'Leibnitz Beta Plateau' box (Zenodo midpoint -85.4258/31.8273), i.e. a rename after IAU naming; the peak reaches ~6000 m and descends to ~5000 m toward the pole (Astronomy.com). Overlaps the Nobile Rim 1 box on the map. LUPEX/ESA ROI LP1 (85.4596S, 31.78E) nearby.

sites.name: Mons Mouton Plateau
sites.notes: Digitized from NASA's Oct-2024 map: a large box ~78 x 59 km (not 15x15 km) on the flat summit of Mons Mouton (IAU -84.6/31.0, 130 km), north of the 'Mons Mouton' box and adjoining Nobile Rim 1. Elevation 5000-6000 m; widest and flattest Artemis site (~60 km span), high enough for near-perpetual sunlight; sized for expanded Artemis IV/V exploration (Astronomy.com). sites.name: Nobile Rim 1
sites.notes: Bbox midpoint (lon 31.66-43.23, lat -85.90 to -84.98). Same box in 2024 (digitized -85.42/37.3). SW rim of Nobile rising ~3000 m (Astronomy.com). Mazarico 2011 Site 6 / PGDA Site06 'Nobile rim 1'. Adjacent (east) to the Mons Mouton / Leibnitz Beta Plateau region.

sites.name: Nobile Rim 2
sites.notes: Bbox midpoint (lon 54.46-63.02, lat -84.40 to -83.50). Same box on the Oct-2024 NASA map (digitized -83.93/58.7). NE rim of Nobile (IAU -85.28/53.27, 79 km). Elevation about -1400 m, second-lowest Artemis site (Astronomy.com from NASA). ~15x15 km nominal.

sites.name: Peak near Cabeus B
sites.notes: Digitized from NASA's Oct-2024 region map (box ~21 km; ~193 km from pole; NASA/Astronomy.com: ~200 km, most distant region, terrain climbs ~6 km over 30 km; elevation -2900 to +3850 m). Uncertainty ~0.05 deg lat, ~1.5 deg lon. Cabeus B crater IAU center -82.26/-54.58 (59.6 km). Flahaut 2020 'South Cabeus B' ROI (-84.0, -60.5): highest avg Earth visibility of 14 south-polar ROIs (0.55), illuminatio

sites.name: Slater Plain
sites.notes: Digitized from NASA's Oct-2024 map (box ~21 km, ~86 km from pole, far side). Plain NE of Slater crater (IAU -88.08/111.29, 25 km); lowest-elevation Artemis region, rolling hills sloping east to west from ~1800 m to -300 m (Astronomy.com). Far-side longitude implies reduced direct-to-Earth visibility. New in 2024.

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim 2
sites.notes: Bbox midpoint (lon -77.47 to -49.40, lat -88.66 to -87.79). Retained in 2024; closest region to the pole (~50-54 km); rim rises ~3000 m above surroundings (Astronomy.com). Flahaut 2020 'North de Gerlache' ROI (-87.9, -65.1): avg Earth visibility 0.50, illumination 0.32. de Gerlache crater IAU center -88.48/-88.34, 32.7 km, PSR floor.

sites.name: Amundsen Rim
sites.notes: Bounding-box midpoint of the NASA 2022 region polygon (Bertone et al. 2026 PSJ archive, doi 10.5281/zenodo.17954508; bbox lon 65.10-73.51, lat -84.65 to -83.80). Nominal region ~15x15 km (NASA release 22-089). Dropped from the Oct-2024 list. Rim of Amundsen crater (IAU center -84.44/83.07, 103 km). Flahaut 2020 'South Amundsen' ROI (-85.0, 90.0): avg Earth visibility 0.32, avg illumination 0.26. N

sites.notes: Bbox midpoint (lon -171.47 to -101.89, lat -89.84 to -89.09). Dropped in 2024. Ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache = Mazarico 2011 Site 1 / PGDA Site01. sites.name: Connecting Ridge Extension
sites.notes: Bbox midpoint (lon -130.73 to -78.22, lat -89.37 to -88.62); lon midpoint less meaningful this close to the pole. Dropped in 2024. PGDA site SL3. Bertone 2026: SfS DEM reveals sharper high-illumination ridges and more small PSRs here. Extends the Shackleton-de Gerlache ridge toward de Gerlache; Glaser 2018 'Connecting Ridge C2' (-89.3130, 245.98E = -114.02) has 78.1% avg / 82.0% max illumination a

sites.name: Faustini Rim A
sites.notes: Bbox midpoint (lon 79.51-100.49, lat -88.19 to -87.54). Dropped in 2024. Rim/proximal ejecta of Faustini crater (IAU -87.18/84.31, 42 km; PSR floor). PGDA LOLA_5mpp site LM8 'Faustini Rim A'. Flahaut 2020 'Faustini ridge' ROI (-87.6, 103.7): avg Earth visibility 0.31, illumination 0.26; 'Shoemaker-Faustini ridge' (-87.1, 65.4): 0.38/0.26.

sites.name: Leibnitz Beta Plateau
sites.notes: Bbox midpoint (lon 27.29-36.37, lat -85.79 to -85.06). Summit plateau of Leibnitz Beta, named Mons Mouton by IAU (2022/2023). The Oct-2024 map shows the same box relabeled 'Mons Mouton' (digitized -85.40/31.6). Mazarico 2011 Site 20 / PGDA Site20. LUPEX/ESA ROI LP1 (85.4596S, 31.78E) chosen for high illumination and strong Earth visibility (Hemmi 2025). VIPER's Mons Mouton site is in this vicinity

sites.name: Peak Near Shackleton
sites.notes: Bbox midpoint (lon 107.53-141.84, lat -89.17 to -88.44). Dropped in 2024. Isolated far-side peak between Shackleton and Slater = Mazarico 2011 Site 7 / PGDA Site07 / Kumari 2022 Site 007 (dense boulder field near a large PSR). Bussey 2010 point D 88.79S/124.5E: 86% illuminated in 2020 (58-100% per lunar day). Flahaut 2020 'Near Shackleton' ROI (-88.6, 101.4): avg Earth visibility 0.39. SpaceNews:

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim 1
sites.notes: Archive label is 'de Gerlache Rim' (ID 9; bbox lon -81.16 to -51.58, lat -89.02 to -88.33); identified as Rim 1 because it contains Mazarico Site 11 / Kumari Site 011 (UAF: Site 011 is in de Gerlache Rim 1) and Bussey point C 88.71S/68.7W (85% illuminated in 2020, min 64%). Dropped in 2024. LUPEX candidate GR1 (88.6952S, 291.7154E) lies here. Boulder fields near the most-illuminated point (Kumari

sites.name: de Gerlache-Kocher Massif
sites.notes: Bbox midpoint (lon -122.59 to -110.48, lat -86.27 to -85.39). Dropped in 2024. Far-side massif between de Gerlache and Kocher (IAU -84.47/-134.02, 24 km); PGDA Site42. Used as the example region in Bertone 2026 (PGDA product 104). Far-side location implies limited direct Earth visibility.

sites.name: Amundsen crater (center)
sites.notes: IAU center, diameter 103.39 km; Artemis 2022 Amundsen Rim region on its rim; Flahaut 2020 South Amundsen ROI.

sites.name: Cabeus (LCROSS Centaur impact site)
sites.notes: Target impact point (84.675S, 311.275E) as of 8 Oct 2009; shepherding spacecraft 84.729S/310.64E; impact 9 Oct 2009 11:31 UTC inside the permanently shadowed part of Cabeus; water detected in the ejecta plume (Colaprete 2010). Cabeus crater IAU center -85.3303/-42.1327 (100.58 km; Wikipedia gives older 84.9S/35.5W).

sites.name: Cabeus B crater (center)
sites.notes: IAU satellite feature (305.4154E), diameter 59.62 km; namesake of the 2024 'Peak near Cabeus B' region (~70 km to its SW).

sites.name: Cabeus crater (center)
sites.notes: IAU center (317.8673E), diameter 100.58 km; PSR floor with LCROSS-confirmed volatiles; ~60 km floor. Wueller et al. 2025 geologic map covers Mons Mouton, Mons Malapert and Cabeus.

sites.name: Chang'e-7 target (illuminated rim of Shackleton)
sites.notes: CNSA/NSSC (Wang et al. 2023, NSR, doi 10.1093/nsr/nwad329) state the lander will land on the illuminated rim of Shackleton; final site not announced. The 88.8S/123.4E value is Wikipedia's ('Peak near the southeast ridge of Shackleton', citing a Weibo post) and coincides with NASA's Peak Near Shackleton region (-88.81/124.68). Landing accuracy <100 m; Queqiao-2 relay used because Earth visibility i

sites.name: Connecting Ridge C1 (peak)
sites.notes: Best-lit point on the ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache (Gläser et al. 2018, site C1): 88.0% average illumination at 2 m over 20 years; longest shadow 112 h.

sites.name: Faustini crater (center)
sites.notes: IAU center, diameter 42.48 km, PSR floor; rim hosts Artemis 2022 region Faustini Rim A.

sites.name: Haworth crater (center)
sites.notes: IAU center (354.83E), diameter 51.42 km, PSR floor adjacent to the Artemis Haworth region.

sites.name: ISRO/JAXA LUPEX target (Shackleton-de Gerlache ridge, candidate CR1)
sites.notes: No official site yet. ISRO (Dagar et al., LPSC 2024 #1898, hou.usra.edu/meetings/lpsc2024/pdf/1898.pdf) describes the proposed LUPEX site on the Shackleton-de Gerlache ridge (OHRC image centred 89.2836S, 140.556W). JAXA JLPEDA lists six LUPEX candidate sites with 1 m DTMs (Hemmi et al. 2025 PSJ 6:264, Table 1): CR1 -89.4679/-137.411 (connecting ridge; this entry), GR1 -88.6952/-68.2846, GR2 -89.00

sites.name: Intuitive Machines IM-2 Athena landing site (Mons Mouton)
sites.notes: Actual touchdown 6 Mar 2025 inside a ~20 m crater, lander on its side (LROC NAC, 10 Mar 2025). Intended site -84.78/29.13E, 160 km from the pole, 'in the central portion of one of the Artemis 3 potential landing regions' (LROC page 1401) - i.e. the 2024 Mons Mouton Plateau region. Mons Mouton thought to be part of the SPA basin rim; ~6 km high plateau (DLR).

sites.name: Kocher crater (center)
sites.notes: IAU center (225.9756E), diameter 24.03 km; namesake of the 2022 de Gerlache-Kocher Massif region.

sites.name: Malapert crater (center)
sites.notes: IAU center, diameter 72.38 km; Malapert A (NE) was the IM-1 landing area (Feb 2024).

sites.name: Nobile crater (center)
sites.notes: IAU center, diameter 79.27 km; interior almost permanently shadowed; Artemis regions Nobile Rim 1 (SW rim) and Nobile Rim 2 (NE rim); VIPER/Griffin target on its western rim (Mons Mouton).

sites.name: Shackleton crater (center)
sites.notes: IAU Gazetteer center, diameter 20.92 km; the south pole lies on its rim. Simple bowl, ~4 km deep, 30.5 deg wall slopes; large PSR on the floor (Wang et al. 2023 NSR). Target area of Chang'e-7 (illuminated rim) and ISRO/JAXA LUPEX.

sites.name: Shackleton rim (best-lit point)
sites.notes: Glaser et al. 2018 Table 1, surface level, 20-year average: 81.0% avg illumination, 85.5% max solar visibility, longest shadow 221 h; at 2 m height the best point shifts to -89.7815/204.70E(-155.30): 82.1%/89.8%, 65 h; cluster S0 85.5%/89.4%. Other studies: Mazarico 2011 -89.78/204.27E (86.7%/90.5%); Speyerer & Robinson 2013 -89.740/201.2E (94% of a lunar year at best rim sites); Bussey 2010 point

sites.name: Shoemaker crater
sites.notes: IAU center, diameter 51.82 km, PSR floor (hydrogen-rich). PGDA LOLA_5mpp includes a Shoemaker DEM and 'Shoemaker Rims A-F' sites; Flahaut 2020 'Shoemaker-Faustini ridge' ROI (-87.1, 65.4): Earth visibility 0.38, illumination 0.26, highest H abundance of the 14 ROIs.

sites.name: Slater crater (center)
sites.notes: IAU center, diameter 25.12 km, approved 2015; namesake of the 2024 Slater Plain region (~35 km to its NE).

sites.name: South Pole (90° S)
sites.notes: Reference point at the pole, on the rim of Shackleton crater. Latitude stored as −89.9999° so that north is defined along the 0° meridian.

sites.name: Sverdrup crater
sites.notes: IAU center (206.6125E), diameter 32.83 km, PSR floor; far side of the pole. Flahaut 2020 ROIs: North Sverdrup (-87.4, -148.2) avg Earth visibility 0.21; West Sverdrup (-88.0, 173.2) 0.33, illumination 0.29. Zhao 2025 lists Sverdrup-BR among higher-illumination CE-7 landing regions.

sites.name: VIPER planned site (Mons Mouton, west of Nobile)
sites.notes: NASA (20 Sep 2021): VIPER to land in the mountainous area near the western edge of Nobile crater; SVS 5074: 'on Mons Mouton, near the western rim of Nobile'; Nobile study region ~93 km2, 16-24 km traverse, ~100 days, solar power with DTE comms (Earth below horizon ~half of each month -> safe havens). No coordinates published by NASA; this preset uses the Mons Mouton summit region (2022 Leibnitz Be

sites.name: de Gerlache crater (center)
sites.notes: IAU center (271.6553E), diameter 32.71 km, PSR floor (deepest part -2.2 km; CE-7 candidate cold trap).

sites.name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
sites.notes: Lunar module Eagle descent stage, 0°40′27″N 23°28′23″E (LROC-located). First crewed landing, 20 July 1969, Mare Tranquillitatis.

sites.name: Apollo 12 (Ocean of Storms)
sites.notes: Lunar module Intrepid descent stage, 3°00′45″S 23°25′18″W, next to Surveyor 3.

sites.name: Apollo 14 (Fra Mauro)
sites.notes: Lunar module Antares descent stage, 3°38′43″S 17°28′17″W.

sites.name: Apollo 15 (Hadley–Apennine)
sites.notes: Lunar module Falcon descent stage, 26°07′56″N 3°38′02″E, between Hadley Rille and the Apennine mountains.

sites.name: Apollo 16 (Descartes Highlands)
sites.notes: Lunar module Orion descent stage, 8°58′23″S 15°30′01″E.

sites.name: Apollo 17 (Taurus–Littrow)
sites.notes: Lunar module Challenger descent stage, 20°11′27″N 30°46′18″E, in a valley between massifs.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus (near Malapert A)
sites.notes: Intuitive Machines Nova-C, landed 22 Feb 2024 at 80.13°S 1.44°E on a ~12° slope east of Malapert A (LROC imaging). First CLPS landing.

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 (Mons Latreille)
sites.notes: Firefly Blue Ghost lander, landed 2 March 2025 near Mons Latreille in Mare Crisium, 18°33′44″N 61°48′37″E.

sites.name: IM-3 target (Reiner Gamma swirl)
sites.notes: Intuitive Machines IM-3 target region, the Reiner Gamma magnetic swirl; approximate centre of the feature, not a published landing point.

sites.name: Chang'e 3 (Mare Imbrium)
sites.notes: CNSA lander with the Yutu rover, landed 14 Dec 2013, 44°07′N 19°31′W.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 (far side, Von Kármán)
sites.notes: CNSA lander, first far-side landing, 3 Jan 2019, 45°27′22″S 177°35′19″E. Earth is never in view from the far side.

sites.name: Chang'e 5 (Oceanus Procellarum)
sites.notes: CNSA sample-return descent stage, 1 Dec 2020, 43°03′27″N 51°54′58″W.

sites.name: Chang'e 6 (far side, Apollo basin)
sites.notes: CNSA far-side sample return, landed 1 June 2024; LROC position 41.6385°S 206.0148°E (153.9852°W).

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram (high southern latitude)
sites.notes: ISRO lander, 23 Aug 2023, 69°22′23″S 32°19′08″E; the first landing at high southern latitude.

sites.name: SLIM (Shioli crater, JAXA)
sites.notes: JAXA precision lander, 19 Jan 2024, 13°18′58″S 25°15′04″E; landed on its nose, which limited solar power.

sites.name: Luna 9 (first soft landing)
sites.notes: USSR, first soft landing on the Moon, 3 Feb 1966, 7°05′N 64°22′W in Oceanus Procellarum.
